The agreement aims to pool expertise and resources to accelerate technological innovation.
Signature d'un accord historique pour l': Signing of a historic agreement for Algerian agriculture
Le Centre de recherche en technologies a: The Research Center in Agro-Food Technologies (CRTAA) of Bejaia formalized, on Wednesday, July 1, 2026, a strategic partnership with the National Institute for Agronomic Research (INRA). This agreement is part of a shared desire to strengthen synergies between the two institutions to address the contemporary challenges of the Algerian agricultural sector. Targeted areas include yield improvement, production chain optimization, and the introduction of innovative technologies into agro-food processes.
Les responsables du CRTAA précisent que: CRTAA officials specify that this collaboration will make it possible to capitalize on the technological advancements developed by the center, particularly in the sectors of agricultural product processing and the valorization of by-products. INRA, for its part, will contribute its expertise in fundamental and applied research, with a particular focus on varieties resistant to climate change and crop diseases. Both parties agreed to establish joint research programs and form mixed teams to successfully carry out these projects.

Ce partenariat revêt une importance capi: This partnership is of paramount importance for Algerian agriculture, a key sector of the national economy. Algeria, with its 58 wilayas, possesses considerable agricultural potential, but faces major challenges such as water scarcity, desertification, and the need to modernize farming techniques. The integration of advanced technologies, such as precision agriculture, smart irrigation, or biotechnology, could significantly improve the sector's productivity and competitiveness.
Dans le contexte actuel, marqué par les: In the current context, marked by the effects of climate change and fluctuations in raw material prices, such collaboration between public research institutions proves essential. It could also serve as a lever to attract private investment in the agro-food industry, a rapidly expanding sector in Algeria. The expected benefits concern not only increased yields, but also the creation of skilled jobs and the development of integrated local value chains.

Les deux institutions ont prévu de lance: The two institutions plan to launch the first joint research projects as early as September 2026, with an initial budget of 200 million Algerian dinars allocated by the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Development. Priority areas include the development of drought-resistant cereal varieties, the optimization of agricultural product preservation techniques, and the creation of digital platforms for food traceability.

Research results will be shared with sector stakeholders via workshops and seminars organized in several wilayas across the country. In the longer term, both parties plan to extend this partnership to other research centers and Algerian universities, in order to create a national ecosystem dedicated to agricultural innovation.
